title: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition) · Units 33–34

units.title: Unit 33 — Academic writing 2: structuring an argument
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 70–71 (PDF pages 74–75).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
units.category: Topics: Work and study · structuring academic arguments
learningObjectives: Organise an academic argument using natural structures for reference, distinction, questions and consideration of evidence.
Strengthen or qualify claims by assessing significance, citing support and marking conviction.
Present, compare and challenge positions using conventional argumentation verbs, adverbs and prepositions.
Correct frequent learner errors in academic phrasing without copying the source exercises.

items.pt: enquadrar-se em categorias; dividir-se em categorias
items.example: These communication errors fall into three broad categories.
items.note: Fall into describes the way examples are classified into groups; it is not a literal fall.

items.pt: fazer referência a; mencionar
items.example: The introduction makes reference to earlier work on renewable energy.
items.note: A relatively formal way to mention a text, person or topic; use make reference to, not give reference to.

items.pt: estabelecer uma distinção entre
items.example: The report draws a distinction between systematic and random errors.
items.note: Means clearly show the difference between two concepts; the preposition is between.

items.pt: levantar questões importantes
items.example: The latest findings raise important questions about long-term safety.
items.note: Questions are raised when a subject is brought up for discussion or investigation.

items.pt: abordar brevemente uma questão
items.example: The literature review touches on an issue that deserves further investigation.
items.note: Touch on means mention or discuss briefly rather than examine thoroughly.

items.pt: levar em consideração
items.example: We should take temperature changes into consideration when analysing the readings.
items.note: Used when including a relevant factor in a decision or argument; take a factor into consideration.

items.pt: defender; apresentar argumentos a favor de
items.example: The author makes a case for using open-source measurement tools.
items.note: Means present reasons in support of a proposal, not merely describe it.

items.pt: reexaminar as evidências
items.example: The researchers decided to re-examine the evidence after new measurements appeared.
items.note: Re-examine means consider existing evidence again, often in response to new information.

items.word: in the light of new evidence
items.pt: à luz de novas evidências
items.example: The committee revised its recommendation in the light of new evidence.
items.note: In the light of means taking new facts or circumstances into account; standard British spelling is light, not lite.

items.word: a leading figure in the field
items.pt: uma figura de destaque na área
items.example: She became a leading figure in the field of robotics through her research.
items.note: Leading figure refers to a prominent expert or influential person in a discipline.

items.pt: avaliar a importância de; avaliar a relevância de
items.example: We need to assess the significance of the difference between the two results.
items.note: Assess means judge the importance or meaning of something using appropriate evidence.

items.pt: dar ênfase a; enfatizar
items.example: The lecturer lays emphasis on reproducible experimental methods.
items.note: A formal alternative to put emphasis on; the pattern is lay emphasis on something.

items.pt: dar respaldo a; apoiar
items.example: These simulations lend support to the proposed explanation.
items.note: Common with evidence, findings or statistics that make an argument more credible.

items.word: lend support to the view that
items.pt: corroborar a visão de que; reforçar o entendimento de que
items.example: Recent survey data lend support to the view that flexible schedules can help productivity.
items.note: This phrase carefully links evidence to a particular interpretation without claiming proof.

items.pt: manter-se firme em uma convicção
items.example: The researcher continues to hold firmly to a belief in open scientific data.
items.note: Hold firmly to signals strong commitment to a belief or position, even if it is challenged.

items.pt: estabelecer uma analogia entre
items.example: The teacher draws an analogy between a feedback loop and a thermostat.
items.note: An analogy explains one thing by comparing it with another that shares relevant features.

items.pt: traçar paralelos entre; apontar semelhanças entre
items.example: The review draws parallels between the two engineering projects.
items.note: Parallels are similarities; this phrase does not claim that the cases are identical.

items.pt: apresentar os argumentos a favor de
items.example: The article presents the case for updating the testing standards.
items.note: A formal phrase for setting out the arguments supporting an idea; compare make a case for.

items.pt: apresentar um argumento; propor uma linha de argumentação
items.example: The authors put forward an argument for collecting more field data.
items.note: Put forward means offer an idea for others to consider, rather than establish it as fact.

items.pt: assumir um posicionamento; adotar uma posição
items.example: The essay takes up a position that many historians would dispute.
items.note: Here position means an intellectual stance, not a job or a physical location.

items.pt: adotar uma posição; assumir um ponto de vista
items.example: The researchers adopt a position based on the precautionary principle.
items.note: Adopt is a natural verb for an academic stance; adapt a position means something different.

items.pt: expressar uma opinião; declarar um ponto de vista
items.example: The writer states an opinion before explaining the supporting evidence.
items.note: State means express clearly or explicitly; it does not imply that the opinion is proven.

items.pt: argumentar de maneira convincente
items.example: The paper argues convincingly that the error cannot be ignored.
items.note: Convincingly evaluates the persuasiveness of reasoning; do not confuse it with convinced.

items.pt: chamar a atenção para
items.example: The article draws attention to gaps in the existing data.
items.note: This phrase directs a reader's notice to a particular issue or finding.

items.pt: pesquisas sugerem uma relação; pesquisas indicam uma possível conexão
items.example: Research suggests a link between sleep habits and concentration.
items.note: Suggests presents an evidence-based possibility, not an absolute conclusion.

items.pt: resumir brevemente
items.example: The final section will briefly summarise the main findings.
items.note: Briefly is the natural adverb with summarise; shortly summarise is not idiomatic in this sense.

items.pt: discordar profundamente
items.example: The reviewers disagree profoundly about the meaning of the results.
items.note: Profoundly conveys major intellectual disagreement; highly disagree is not the normal expression.

items.pt: tirar uma conclusão; chegar a uma conclusão
items.example: After reviewing the evidence, the team was ready to draw a conclusion.
items.note: Use draw or reach with conclusion; a well-supported conclusion follows from the reasoning presented.

items.pt: apresentar argumentos sólidos a favor de
items.example: The report makes a strong case for regular equipment inspections.
items.note: Strong expresses the force of the reasoning and is more emphatic than make a case for alone.

items.pt: levantar questões centrais
items.example: The comparison raises key questions about the reliability of the measurements.
items.note: Key questions are especially important to the central issue.

items.pt: transmitir um argumento; comunicar uma ideia com clareza
items.example: The speaker managed to put across a point about the system's limitations.
items.note: Put across means communicate successfully so that an audience understands.

items.pt: não fazer menção a; não citar
items.example: The abstract makes no reference to the earlier pilot study.
items.note: The negative form highlights an omission, often relevant when evaluating academic writing.

units.title: Unit 34 — Laws and punishments
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 72–73 (PDF pages 76–77).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
units.category: Topics: Society and institutions · law and punishment
learningObjectives: Describe laws being proposed, passed, observed, enforced or broken using the correct verbs.
Use appropriate formal and everyday constructions with rules, permission and regulations.
Describe investigations, court proceedings, verdicts and legal disputes precisely.
Distinguish penalties and their consequences using natural adjective–noun and verb–noun collocations.

items.pt: obedecer à lei; cumprir a lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: Companies must obey the law when handling personal information.
items.note: A neutral everyday expression for doing what legislation requires.

items.pt: observar a lei; cumprir a lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: Public institutions are expected to observe the law in all their decisions.
items.note: More formal than obey the law; observe here means follow, not look at.

items.pt: respeitar a lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: The organisation expects all employees to respect the law.
items.note: Respect suggests treating the law as authoritative and worthy of compliance.

items.pt: infringir a lei; violar a lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: The firm could break the law if it ignores these safety requirements.
items.note: Means act illegally; break a rule may also refer to nonlegal rules.

items.pt: apresentar uma nova lei; instituir uma nova lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: The government plans to introduce a new law on waste management.
items.note: Introduce can mean propose or bring a law into use, depending on the legislative context.

items.pt: aprovar uma lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: Parliament may pass a law requiring clearer product labels.
items.note: Pass a law means approve it through the lawmaking process, not simply suggest it.

items.pt: agir dentro da lei; agir legalmente
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: The company sought legal advice to ensure it acted within the law.
items.note: Formal expression meaning stay within what legislation allows.

items.pt: fazer cumprir a lei; defender a aplicação da lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: The authorities are responsible for upholding the law.
items.note: Uphold means support and maintain respect for legal requirements.

items.pt: fazer cumprir a lei; aplicar a lei
items.section: A · Verbs that collocate with law
items.example: Police officers have a duty to enforce the law fairly.
items.note: Enforce focuses on ensuring compliance, sometimes through penalties or legal powers.

items.pt: a lei proíbe fumar
items.example: In this fictional example, the law forbids smoking in enclosed public spaces.
items.note: Forbid means not allow; it can be followed by an -ing form or by someone plus to-infinitive.

items.pt: a lei proíbe discriminação; a legislação veda discriminação
items.example: The law prohibits discrimination in recruitment in this fictional setting.
items.note: Prohibit is relatively formal; laws prohibit an activity or practice, often expressed with a noun or -ing form.

items.pt: as regras permitem o acesso
items.example: The rules permit access to shared equipment after safety training.
items.note: Permit is relatively formal and can take an object plus to-infinitive.

items.pt: as regras permitem a entrada
items.example: The rules allow entry after an orientation session.
items.note: Allow is more everyday than permit; allow someone to do something is also natural.

items.pt: as regras se aplicam a todos
items.example: The rules apply to everyone who enters the laboratory.
items.note: Apply to identifies the people or situations governed by a rule.

items.pt: seguir as regras; cumprir as regras
items.example: Please follow the rules when using shared equipment.
items.note: A common everyday expression; the verb is follow, not accompany.

items.pt: os regulamentos exigem inspeção
items.example: The regulations require inspection of equipment before use.
items.note: A formal pattern for mandated actions; require that a person do something and require someone to do something are also possible.

items.pt: os regulamentos estipulam um prazo
items.example: The regulations stipulate a deadline for submitting the report.
items.note: Stipulate is formal and emphasises an explicit provision or condition; stipulate that is also common.

items.pt: cumprir os regulamentos; estar em conformidade com as normas
items.example: Suppliers must comply with the regulations on electrical safety.
items.note: Comply takes with, not to; commonly used in technical and legal contexts.

items.pt: flexibilizar as regras; abrir uma exceção às regras
items.example: The organiser agreed to bend the rules for a participant with special circumstances.
items.note: Usually informal: relax a rule in a limited way rather than openly ignore the entire system.

items.pt: realizar uma investigação
items.example: The authorities will carry out an investigation into the incident.
items.note: Carry out is the usual verb for organising and conducting an investigation.

items.pt: comparecer em juízo; comparecer ao tribunal
items.example: The witness is due to appear in court next week.
items.note: Means attend a court hearing as a witness, defendant or other participant.

items.pt: ir a julgamento; começar a ser julgado
items.example: The accused is expected to go on trial in November.
items.note: Means start being tried in court, not simply attend as a witness.

items.pt: chegar a um veredicto
items.example: The jury needed more time to reach a verdict.
items.note: Reach is a natural verb for a jury's final decision on guilt or innocence.

items.pt: um julgamento justo
items.example: Every defendant should have the right to a fair trial.
items.note: Refers to a legally fair process, independent of whether someone is guilty.

items.pt: ser considerado culpado; ter a culpa reconhecida judicialmente
items.example: The defendant was found guilty after the evidence was presented.
items.note: Found guilty describes the judgment reached, not simply an accusation.

items.pt: um veredicto de culpado
items.example: The jury returned a verdict of guilty in the fictional case.
items.note: A specific decision on guilt; the legal procedure varies across jurisdictions.

items.pt: ser punido severamente
items.example: The organisation warned that deliberate fraud would be severely punished.
items.note: Severely intensifies the strength of a punishment, not the seriousness of the offence itself.

items.pt: pagar uma multa elevada
items.example: Drivers may have to pay a heavy fine for repeated offences.
items.note: Heavy is the normal adjective for a large fine; a strong fine is not idiomatic.

items.pt: estar sujeito a uma multa elevada
items.example: Businesses that ignore the rule could face a heavy fine.
items.note: Face highlights a possible penalty, while pay describes actually making the payment.

items.pt: estar sujeito à pena de morte
items.example: In some jurisdictions, a person convicted of certain crimes may face the death penalty.
items.note: This describes a possible legal consequence in certain places; it is not a universal sentence.

items.pt: funcionar como fator de dissuasão; servir para desencorajar
items.example: Visible safety checks can act as a deterrent to deliberate rule-breaking.
items.note: A deterrent is something that discourages unwanted behaviour; effectiveness depends on context.

items.pt: sofrer as consequências
items.example: The contractor had to suffer the consequences of ignoring the contract terms.
items.note: A common expression for experiencing unwelcome results of an action.

items.pt: uma punição severa; uma penalidade rigorosa
items.example: The committee considered the proposed suspension a harsh penalty.
items.note: Harsh suggests severity that may be seen as excessive, depending on context.

items.pt: uma sentença severa; uma pena rigorosa
items.example: The lawyer argued that the defendant had received a harsh sentence.
items.note: Sentence refers to a punishment formally imposed by a court, not a grammatical sentence.

items.pt: uma disputa judicial difícil; uma longa batalha jurídica
items.example: The two parties faced a hard legal battle over the patent.
items.note: Battle is figurative; the phrase refers to a difficult legal dispute.

items.pt: ganhar uma causa; vencer um processo judicial
items.example: The team hopes to win a case against a supplier over faulty equipment.
items.note: In legal contexts, case refers to proceedings or a dispute, not a physical container.

items.pt: sociedades em que as leis são amplamente respeitadas
items.example: Law-abiding societies generally expect public officials to act within the law.
items.note: Law-abiding describes a strong general pattern of obeying laws; it need not suggest that offences never occur.
